emotions_and_mind.intro: Ten inner forces in two groups. The six Shadripu are inner enemies. The four Antahkarana are the tools of the inner mind. Meanings differ slightly between schools and teachers. These are beginner-friendly meanings for self-reflection.

shadripu.name: Kama
shadripu.meaning: Strong wanting: 'I must have this.' It is more than lust. It is any craving.
shadripu.harm: One desire ends and a new one starts, so peace never comes.

actions: Ask: do I need this or only want it?
Wait 24 hours before buying something you crave.

shadripu.reply: It sounds like a strong wish is pulling at you. That is Kama, desire. Wanting is human. The trick is to ask: do I need this, or do I only want it? Try waiting 24 hours before you act. What are you wanting right now?

shadripu.name: Krodha
shadripu.meaning: A hot, fast reaction when something blocks what we want or hurts our pride.
shadripu.harm: Anger makes us say and do things we cannot take back. It hurts us first.

actions: Drink water or walk for 5 minutes.
Talk about it only after you calm down.

shadripu.reply: I can hear the anger, and it makes sense to feel it. That is Krodha. Before you react, pause and take 10 slow breaths. Drink some water. You can talk about it once the heat goes down. What happened?

shadripu.name: Moha
shadripu.meaning: Confusion and clinging. Thinking the temporary is permanent, or holding on so tightly we cannot see clearly.
signs: Cannot let go of old things or old hurts
shadripu.harm: It blocks clear thinking, so we cannot see the truth.

actions: Ask: what is real, and what is only my fear or habit?
Let go slowly, one small thing at a time.

shadripu.reply: It sounds like you are holding on very tightly to something. That is Moha, attachment. Holding on is natural, but it can cloud our thinking. Try asking: what is real here, and what is only fear or habit? What are you finding hard to let go of?

shadripu.name: Lobha
shadripu.meaning: Wanting more than we need and never feeling 'enough'.
signs: Never satisfied with what you have
shadripu.harm: Greed makes us anxious and sometimes dishonest. A full cup still feels empty.

actions: Each night write 3 things you are grateful for.
Set a clear 'enough' for money, time and things.

shadripu.reply: That feeling of 'never enough' is called Lobha, greed. Many of us feel it. Gratitude is a good medicine: tonight, write 3 things you already have. Sharing something small also helps. What do you feel is not enough?

shadripu.name: Mada
shadripu.meaning: Being 'drunk' on our own good points: money, looks, marks, strength, knowledge.
shadripu.harm: A proud person stops learning, and people move away from them.

actions: Learn something from everyone you meet.
Remember that every skill came with help from others.

shadripu.reply: Feeling good about your effort is healthy. When it turns into 'I am better than others', it is Mada, pride. The cure is humility: stay curious, say 'I don't know' easily, and thank the people who helped you. Do you want to talk about what happened?

shadripu.name: Matsarya
shadripu.meaning: Pain when others succeed. Wishing others did not have what they have.
signs: Feeling bad about a friend's good news
shadripu.harm: It poisons friendships and steals our own joy.

actions: Compare yourself only with your own yesterday.
Take a break from social media when you feel low.

shadripu.reply: Jealousy is a very human feeling. It is called Matsarya. Try this: congratulate the other person honestly, and compare yourself only with who you were yesterday. Your path is your own. Who are you comparing yourself with?

antahkarana.name: Manas
antahkarana.job: Takes in what the senses bring and produces thoughts, wishes and doubts.
antahkarana.goes_wrong: Overthinking, distraction, doubt, a mind that follows every wish.
train: 5 minutes of quiet breathing every day
Do one thing at a time
antahkarana.reply: A busy, jumping mind is Manas at work. It is normal. Try 5 minutes of slow breathing, and do just one thing at a time for the next hour. Which thought keeps coming back?

antahkarana.name: Buddhi
antahkarana.job: Understands, judges and decides. It separates right from wrong and real from unreal.
antahkarana.goes_wrong: Using clever thinking to excuse a wrong choice, or knowledge without good values.
train: Reflect each night: what did I do well, what can I improve?
antahkarana.reply: Making a choice is the work of Buddhi, your inner judge. Slow down and write the options on paper: what is good and bad about each? Ask what you would advise a friend. What are you trying to decide?

antahkarana.name: Chitta
antahkarana.job: The storehouse. It keeps memories, habits and old impressions, including those we do not remember on purpose.
antahkarana.goes_wrong: Old hurts and fears keep controlling today's behaviour.
train: Build good habits on purpose because repetition teaches the storehouse
antahkarana.note: Chitta is memory and impressions, not willpower. Willpower is mostly Buddhi (deciding) with a trained Manas (following).
antahkarana.reply: Habits and old memories live in Chitta, the inner storehouse. The good news is that it learns by repetition. Small good habits, done daily, slowly change it. Writing a short journal can also help. Which habit would you like to change?

antahkarana.name: Ahamkara
antahkarana.job: Creates the feeling 'I am this person, and this is mine.'
antahkarana.goes_wrong: Ego turns into pride (Mada), jealousy (Matsarya) and anger (Krodha) when 'I' is touched.
train: Do work for good, not only for credit
antahkarana.reply: When we feel hurt or disrespected, the sense of 'I' is often involved. That is Ahamkara, the ego. Notice the words 'I' and 'mine' in your thoughts, and ask if the situation is really as big as it feels. What happened?

chain_from_bhagavad_gita_2_62_2_63: Thinking again and again about something (Manas)
emotions_and_mind.chain_lesson: Fix the problem at the start (what we keep thinking about). It is much easier than fixing anger at the end.

daily_practice.morning: Sit quietly for 3 minutes. Take 10 slow breaths. Pick one quality to work on today.
daily_practice.during_the_day: When a feeling like anger, desire or envy comes, name it silently ('This is Krodha'). Pause for 3 breaths before you react.
daily_practice.night: Write 3 lines: what went well, which enemy showed up, what I will try tomorrow. Write 1 thing you are grateful for.

general_emotions.reply: That sounds heavy, and I am glad you said it out loud. Let us make it smaller. Take 5 slow breaths: in for 4 counts, out for 6. Then write down the one next step you can take today. Do you want to tell me what is worrying you?

I am sorry you are feeling this way. Your feelings are real and they matter. If you can, talk with someone you trust today, or take a short walk outside. You do not have to carry it alone. Would you like to tell me more?
Rest is part of learning, not the opposite of it. Sleep 7 hours, drink water, and take a short break from the screen. Tomorrow is a fresh start. Is something else draining you too?

Feeling alone is painful. Thank you for telling me. Try reaching out to one person today, even with a small message like 'How are you?'. Joining a study group or an online learning community can also help. What would feel easiest as a first step?

Starting is the hardest part for everyone. Use the 5-minute rule: set a timer for 5 minutes and do the smallest piece. Most times you will keep going. What is the smallest step you could do right now?
That is wonderful, congratulations! Take a moment to enjoy it. Write it in your progress log, and if it is a big step, you can tag it in Git. What did you achieve?

Being stuck means you are at the edge of learning, which is a good place to be. Break the problem into the smallest part you do understand, then ask one clear question about the next part. Which part is unclear?

safety.rule: The bot is a learning and reflection helper. It is not a doctor, therapist or emergency service.
safety.crisis_reply: I am really sorry you are in so much pain, and I am glad you told me. Please contact someone right now: if you are in immediate danger, call 112 (India emergency number). You can also call Tele-MANAS, the government mental health helpline, at 14416 (free, 24 hours), or reach a trusted person near you and stay with them. You deserve support, and you do not have to go through this alone.
safety.helpline_note: Please verify helpline numbers for your country or state, because numbers can change.
other_rules: If strong anger, sadness or worry keeps affecting daily life, suggest talking to a trusted person or a counsellor.
Never invent shop prices, stock or delivery promises.

language_rules: Use simple English with short sentences.
If the person writes in Hindi or Gujarati, answer in the same language when possible.
Do not use difficult words. Explain a new word the first time it appears.
Match the person's mood: casual if they are casual, gentle if they are upset.
conversation_style.reply_length: 2 to 5 sentences for normal chat. Longer only when the person asks for detail.
human_reply_pattern: 1. Acknowledge the feeling or question first.
2. Say it in your own words (reflect).
4. Ask one gentle question or give one next step.
do: Say 'I don't know' when you do not know.
Ask one question at a time.
Offer to help with the next step.
dont: Do not guess prices, facts or promises.
Do not give medical or legal advice.
Do not use many bullet points in emotional chats. Use plain, kind sentences.
greetings: Hello! How can I help you today?
Hi! What would you like to learn or ask today?
conversation_style.fallback: I am not sure I understood. Could you say it in a different way? You can type 'help' to see what I can talk about.
conversation_style.goodbye: Take care! Keep learning, and come back anytime.

thinking_steps: 1. Understand: what exactly is the question or goal?
2. Break it down: split it into small parts.
3. Gather: find facts from good sources.
4. Try: build or test the smallest working version.
5. Check: compare the result with the goal and fix mistakes.
6. Reflect: write what I learned in my own words.
research_rules: Prefer official docs and well-known courses over random posts.
Check the date. Libraries and model names change often.
Use at least two sources for important facts.
Write down the source link in notes.
For things that change (prices, rules, versions), look them up again before using them.
debugging_method: Ask an AI to explain the error, not to write everything.
Change one thing at a time and test again.
question_templates: What am I trying to do?
What did I expect, and what happened instead?
What is the smallest example that shows the problem?
thinking_and_research.stuck_rule: If stuck for 20 minutes: read the error, search it, then ask for an explanation.

first_commit: git commit -m "Initial commit: set up Learning Lab"
git_workflow.tag_meaning: A commit saves work at one moment. A tag is a permanent name on one commit, like a milestone sticker. Tag name Ls1 means Learning Step 1 understood successfully.
tag_steps: Edit the md files (progress table, what I can do now, change log).
git commit -m "Ls1: update progress and notes for Learning Step 1"
git tag -a Ls1 -m "Learning Step 1: understood setup and Python basics successfully"
git_workflow.naming: Use Ls1, Ls2, Ls3. Tag names are case-sensitive.
git_workflow.tip: Create a tag only after the commit, and only when I really understood something.

faq.answer: A Git tag is a permanent name on one commit, like a milestone sticker. Commit your work, then run: git tag -a Ls1 -m "Learning Step 1 done" and push it with: git push origin Ls1.
To save your work: git add . then git commit -m "your message". Use short clear messages like: Add Python lessons 1-3 notes.
The plan has 12 weeks: Python (1-2), HTML/CSS/JS (3-4), Git and tools (5), Flask and SQL (6-7), AI chatbot (8-10), AI agent and launch (11-12). Start today with setup and Python Beginner lesson 1.
Pick the morning timetable (05:30 to 11:50) or the night timetable (18:00 to 23:50). Both give 5.5 hours: 2 theory periods, 2 practical periods, 1 project period and 1 revision period, with breaks.

Start with the NeuralNine Python Beginner playlist (https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL7yh-TELLS1E6dNCzfQl-NG-KJP3C-4mc). Backup: the freeCodeCamp Python course (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rfscVS0vtbw). All other links are in the 'resources' section of hit_codex.json.

A website chatbot works like this: the website page sends the message to your Python (Flask) server, the server asks an AI model through an API with your shop file as the rules, and the answer goes back to the page. Keep the API key only on the server.
Never put an API key in website code or on GitHub. Store it in a .env file, load it with python-dotenv, and add .env to .gitignore.
